applicantTitle: TEST J27: A portable sensor for detecting copper in drinking water
layAbstract: We will build a portable device that measures copper in drinking water. The device could help people decide when to send water for a laboratory test. Our tests will measure how accurately it reads copper at different concentrations.
summaryFields:
Scientific Question: Can a portable device detect copper at useful concentrations?
Potential Impact: Provide a device for screening drinking water. Reduce unnecessary laboratory tests.
Risks: Other dissolved metals may interfere with the reading.
Enabling Advances: A benchtop copper probe has been demonstrated.
New Area: Miniaturizing the probe.
Peer Groups: Water sensor developers.
Prior Support: Other Support unavailable.
proposalText:
[page 1]
Project Narrative
The near-term goal is a portable device for screening drinking water. The project will build a handheld reader and compare its accuracy to a laboratory assay. The proposed outcomes are device accuracy and battery life.
[page 2]
Approach
The team has demonstrated a benchtop copper probe. It will integrate the probe with a handheld reader. Other dissolved metals may interfere with the reading.
